newsitem.title: USA: Three firms fined $75 mln in Puerto Rico oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Three firms fined $75 mln in Puerto Rico oil spill.

text.p: A U.S. federal judge on Wednesday slapped a total $75 million fine on three corporations owned by the Frank family of New York for their role in a big oil spill off Puerto Rico in January 1994, the Justice Department said.
The fine was the largest ever for an environmental crime, the department said.

Judge Hector Laffitte of the U.S. District Court for San Juan said "recklessly negligent" conduct by the companies had caused the 750,000 gallon fuel oil spill which fouled waters off a popular beach at the peak of the tourist season.
Bunker Group Puerto Rico, Bunker Group Incorporated, and New England Marine Services were each fined $25 million and were subjected to five years of corporate probation.
The three companies are among 50 units by the Frank family, which has a long record of environmental violations, the Justice Department said.
Pedro Rivera, the general manager of Bunker Group Puerto Rico, is due to be sentenced separately on Thursday.
A federal jury convicted the firms in April for sending out a damaged tugboat, causing an oil spill, and failing to alert the Coast Guard that the vessel was impaired.
